messages:
chris: Heads up — us-west1 scratch nodes (gnode-223/224) are seeing a sustained writeback queue spike. GPU launches delayed, batch jobs piling up.
infra-bot: [ALERT] writeback_queue_depth > 500 on gnode-223, gnode-224. Started 2026-03-20T01:12Z. Monitor: https://internal/mon/alerts/4801234567 :rotating_light:
maria: seeing high avg_q_sz and sda util ~99% on gnode-223. iostat shows huge await and svctm. Jobs are timing out.
chris: any recent kernel or firmware pushes to these hosts?
devin: no infra push in last 6h. docker batch window began ~01:08Z. dmesg on gnode-223 shows repeated:
```
[    72.123456] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev sda, sector 123456
[    72.123789] writeback: stalled for 500ms, order:1 dev sda
```
anya: that looks like writeback stalls + retry churn. Could be parity/metadata stripe fanout causing tiny syncs to serialize.
leo: if parity/metadata writes are landing on same physical LUNs we get head-of-line. Also saw overlayfs fsync storms in prior incidents.
maria: quick checks:
```
# iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rsec/s wsec/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
sda      0.00   0.10 0.20 500.00  10.00 40000.00   160.00    6.20  12.30  0.02 99.00
```
devin: on gnode-224 tail of /var/log/journal shows repeated overlayfs fsync retries and GO_SCHEDULER backpressure logs from our janitor.
anya: can we throttle/disable janitor and ephemeral cleaner on those hosts? Background compaction looks aggressive.
leo: flipping cleaner -> passive on gnode-223/224 now. will increase batching window for writes.
chris: please do. also pause heavy /tmp-churn batch jobs in the next 10m — @platform-scheduler FYI.
platform-scheduler: acknowledged — pausing queued batch windows in us-west1 for 15m.
maria: cleaner stopped on both hosts: systemctl stop ephemeral-cleaner.service -> succeeded :white_check_mark:
devin: after stop, avgqu dropped to ~1.2 and %util down to ~40% within 90s. GPU launches recovering.
chris: root cause hypothesis: concurrent parity/metadata syncs + janitor compaction produced retry storm and writeback serialization on same LUNs.
anya: next steps: 1) isolate metadata IO to separate devices; 2) reduce janitor concurrency per node; 3) add soft-throttle for overlayfs fsync bursts.
leo: opening PR with janitor concurrency defaults + canary rollout to us-west. Will include telemetry tags for writeback_queue_depth.
maria: filing incident note and attaching perf graphs to ticket. tagging this thread #followup
chris: thanks all. re-enable cleaner after PR + canary. will check in 2h unless regressions.
infra-bot: [RUNBOOK] writeback-stall -> https://internal/runbooks/writeback-stall :memo:
